text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 29 in history.
1170 - Thomas a Becket, Archbishop of Canterbury, was murdered by four knights acting on the orders of England's King Henry II.
1800 - Charles Goodyear, American who developed the art of vulcanising rubber, used in the production of car tyres, born.
1808 - Andrew Johnson, 17th U.S. president, born.
1809 - William Gladstone, four times British prime minister, born.
1845 - Texas became the 28th U.S. state.
1859 - The first iron-hulled armoured warship, Britain's HMS Warrior, was launched.
1874 - Alfonso XII was proclaimed king of Spain.
1876 - Pablo Casals, Spanish cellist and conductor, born.
1890 - More than 200 Sioux men, women and children were massacred by U.S. troops at Wounded Knee, South Dakota.
1895 - The Jameson Raid into the Transvaal to aid the Uitlanders (mainly British settlers) in the Boer republic, began.
1911 - Sun Yat Sen became the first president of the Chinese Republic.
1911 - Emil Julius Klaus Fuchs, German physicist who settled in Britain and spied for the Soviet Union, born.
1937 - The constitution of the Republic of Ireland came into effect.
1940 - German aircraft dropped thousands of incendiary bombs on London, destroying some cherished buildings.
1944 - Soviet tanks entered Budapest in World War Two.
1952 - The first transistor hearing aid was marketed in the United States.
1965 - President Ho Chi Minh of North Vietnam rejected unconditional peace talks offered by U.S.
1972 - Ninety-nine people were killed when an Eastern Airlines Lockheed L-1011 crashed into the Everglades near Miami International Airport in Florida.
1975 - A bomb explosion at New York's La Guardia airport killed 11.
1981 - President Reagan announced a programme of economic sanctions against the Soviet Union because of its alleged role in the imposition of martial law in Poland.
1983 - The United States formally announced its intention to withdraw from UNESCO at the end of 1984.
1986 - Former British prime minister (1957-63) Harold Macmillan died.
1989 - Playwright Vaclav Havel, jailed for five years for his human rights activities and long denounced in the communist media as an enemy of the state, was sworn in as president of Czechoslovakia.
1992 - President Daniel arap Moi won Kenya's first multi-party polls in 26 years.
1992 - The Yugoslav parliament voted to oust Prime Minister Milan Panic from office.
1993 - After 2,000 years of often hostile Christian-Jewish relations, the Vatican and Israel approved a document in which the Holy See and the Jewish state recognised each other.
1994 - Fifty-three people were killed when a Turkish Airlines aircraft crashed in a snowstorm while trying to land in eastern Turkey.
1995 - A French air force cargo plane landed at the Bosnian city of Mostar, becoming the first aircraft to do so since 1992.
